approach.method_basis: The reference is Zhu and colleagues' 2022 paper, An Inverse QSAR Method Based on Linear Regression and Integer Programming. The method learns a linear relationship between molecular descriptors and a measured property, then places that predictor and the descriptor equations inside an integer program describing a chemical graph. Atom identities, bonds and structural restrictions are represented by discrete variables and constraints. Solving the combined program constructs a graph whose descriptors satisfy the predictor's requested property range and the structural specifications. Because the descriptors and graph share one constrained assignment, the representation used to predict the property is tied directly to the molecule being constructed.
approach.novelty: This root adapts the published construction framework to online score maximization with limited accepted observations. It refits a regularized linear predictor of whole-molecule atom, degree and typed-bond counts after each accepted batch, then maximizes that prediction while replacing a small, singly attached acyclic peripheral region of a scored molecule. The surrounding context stays fixed; the program chooses replacement size, atom identities, bond orders and a chemically eligible attachment site together. Source selection favors higher observed scores while retaining alternatives. Bounded solves may use feasible incumbents, with repeated assignments excluded and additional construction attempts used to obtain novel molecules. Independent checks require the submitted graph's count descriptors to match the integer model exactly. These choices make exact prediction realization testable within the resource budget, while leaving the usefulness of the linear predictor and construction throughput as separate empirical questions.

observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent. Observation n-0e1f7686dea8 confirms structural gradient optimization and successful context-preserving assembly, but positive relaxed gains sometimes became negative mean predicted gains after discrete assembly. Its chronological prediction errors and negative mean actual source-relative gains also show a distinct predictive-usefulness risk. The proposed integer construction addresses the realization gap by making the optimized descriptor vector and constructed graph agree exactly; it does not assume that linear counts predict these objectives accurately or that exact realization alone improves scores. The additional untested prerequisite is sufficient throughput from chemically feasible, novel integer constructions under the supplied resources.
hypothesis: Fit a task-local regularized linear score model on exact molecular count descriptors, then construct new bounded peripheral regions of scored molecules by maximizing that predictor in a mixed-integer graph program whose atom, bond, attachment, valence, connectivity and descriptor constraints jointly define the submitted molecular graph.

finding_summary.headline: Exact integer realization held for all 1,450 proposals; only 41% of predicted local gains became observed gains
finding_summary.insights: The construction and adaptive feedback mechanisms happened. This result establishes that exact count realization and sufficient integer-construction throughput are attainable in this bounded peripheral-edit domain; the remaining predictive errors cannot be attributed to a mismatch between optimized descriptors and submitted graphs. The representational limit is visible in the accepted data: different molecules with identical full descriptor vectors received different scores on every task. In the docking trajectory, the two fluorine-position variants highlighted by the chemistry assessment share all 384 counts but score 0.124071 and 0.189601. No refit of this descriptor-only linear predictor can distinguish that pair. The chemistry assessment also finds familiar inherited rings carrying many reactive or unconventional appendages, alongside simpler high-scoring alternatives. Together, these observations make richer chemical-environment representation and constraints on functional-group compatibility worth testing while keeping exact realization as a control. They do not establish that either change will improve scores. Current evidence covers neutral, unspecified-stereochemistry peripheral trees and retained ring frameworks; new ring construction, broader chemistry and reliable advantage across replicas remain open.
finding_summary.results: All five tasks completed on the screening seed. The optimizer supplied 145 full batches and 1,450 novel accepted molecules from feasible integer assignments, with zero discrepancies across their 384 count descriptors. All 150 ridge fits reconstructed from accepted task-local scores, and the 140 feedback refits with later opportunities changed subsequent construction objectives. Accepted constructions were selected again as sources 525 times. Of 1,450 proposals, 1,400 had positive predicted gains over their source; 578 of those predictions became actual gains. Overall, 598 proposals beat their source and 36 improved the running best, although mean child-minus-source score was negative on three of the five tasks. The final five-task Top-1 mean was 0.286518. Initial to final Top-1 changed from 0.305105 to 0.395373 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.583606 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.189601 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.175888 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.088123 for sitagliptin_mpo. This root has no Parent, and one screening seed does not establish comparative advantage.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich inherited scaffolds acquire unusual reactive appendages; conventional amides and amines coexist with azo, N-F and thiocarbonyl chemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied trajectories were read, covering every task in the brief. Each contains 300 molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals, on seed 0. There is no Parent or Parent trajectory, so the comparison is with the supplied initial molecules and the observed within-task score gradient. Scores quoted below are rounded recorded values, not new evaluations. The output contains substantial ring chemistry: ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout. The recurrent frameworks are indoles, diaryl fused dione heterocycles, quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine assemblies, biphenyl/arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine assemblies, and oxygen-rich polyacetals. These are recognizable in the initial molecules; much of the subsequent variety changes their substituents while retaining their ring frameworks. Aromatic_atom_rate, which measures the fraction of proposal strings containing aromatic atoms rather than the fraction of atoms that are aromatic, is 0.9586, 0.9897, 0.9966, 1.0 and 0.331 in the fixed task order. The last trajectory develops a predominantly nonaromatic polyacetal series. Thus structural diversity is moderate across the supplied outputs, but the chemically favored series within a task are narrower than the 300 unique identities suggest. Synthetic plausibility is mixed. Familiar amides, ethers, esters, alkylated amines and heterocycles remain available, while many proposals combine N-F, repeated N-O or N-N linkages, sulfur-halogen bonds, unstabilized thiocarbonyls or cumulated double bonds. The recognizable cores do not make these appendages ordinary medicinal chemistry. Every proposal set has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate of 0.0: explicit ions and assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry are absent from the submitted strings, although ionizable atoms and potential stereocentres are present. No synthesis, stability, affinity or protonation-state measurement was supplied.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules are medium-sized, aromatic indole derivatives carrying a fluorophenyl group through a carboxamide or an aminomethyl linker. Methoxy/other ether substituents and the indole NH are recurrent. Evaluation 153 is a comparatively conventional dimethoxyindole carboxamide with an N-methyl-N-fluorophenyl amide; its amide nitrogen is not an ordinary basic amine. Other upper-score examples add N-fluoroaminomethyl ethers, N-ethynyl groups or vinylamine motifs. Lower-score families include elaborate saturated polyacetals and bulkier diaryl fused diones. The optimizer strings have mean length 48.6, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9586 and halogen_rate 0.9483. The best conventional amide looks synthetically plausible in outline; many surrounding analogues are substantially less convincing.
liabilities: N-F-bearing amines, sulfur-fluoride/chloride appendages and heteroatom-substituted alkynes raise stability and route-planning concerns. The aryl C-F bond in the best molecule should not be conflated with these heteroatom-halogen bonds.
Cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1345. Several high-score analogues retain unsaturated or N-F-bearing appendages even though the observed maximum needs neither.
missing_features: The later output does not consistently retain the favorable combination of a small N-alkyl carboxamide and uncomplicated aryl ethers: final analogues frequently replace it with N-F, ethynyl-ether or sulfur-halogen chemistry. The clean combination exists at the maximum, so this is a coverage gap rather than complete inability to make it.

Alternative ring-nitrogen placements and reorganized ring frameworks are not represented among the cited high-score molecules. Their benefit cannot be established from this trajectory, which does not identify a unique missing target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole secondary amide at evaluation 9 scores 0.305105, whereas the dimethoxy N-methyl amide at 153 scores 0.395373. This supports a local preference for that combined substitution change, without separating the effects of losing a methoxy group, its position and amide methylation. The N-F-containing analogue at 160 is nearly equal at 0.394920, so the score tolerates unusual chemistry rather than demonstrating its necessity. The oxygen-rich polycycle at 13 scores 0.0000369102 and the larger fused-dione compound at 95 scores 0.0000487084. Final ethynyl-ether/sulfur-fluoride indoles at 299 and 300 both score 0.0153241. The observed favorable feature is the particular compact indole/aryl/linker combination, not aromaticity or halogenation alone.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by fairly large diaryl fused dione heterocycles with N-methylated ring nitrogens. Their aromatic substituents acquire primary or alkylated amino groups, methylthio groups, fluorinated aminoalkyl branches and azo/diazene substituents. The maximum at 284 combines a fused dione core with densely substituted phenyl rings, dimethylamino functionality, an alpha-fluoroamine branch and repeated azo functionality. A distinct high-score example at 169 instead has amino/methylamino groups, a phenol and an aldehyde, without azo or fluorinated appendages. Indole carboxamides also recur late. Mean SMILES length is 65.4, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9897 and halogen_rate is 0.6621. Familiar cores are present, but the densely decorated azo/aminal-rich periphery often makes the complete molecules questionable synthetic targets.
liabilities: Aryl/alkyl azo groups and terminal diazenes introduce unassigned geometric isomerism and potential redox or decomposition liabilities; repeated N-N units and highly substituted aminal/hemiaminal-like branches are especially unconventional.
Aldehydes, amino-substituted aromatics and methylthio groups still need chemical scrutiny in the simpler series; a high scalar score is not evidence of stability or an executable synthesis.
Fluorinated aminoalkyl branches can introduce stereocentres, but no tetrahedral configuration is specified in these proposal strings.
missing_features: Relatively simple amino/phenol/carbonyl combinations are underrepresented among the heavily decorated upper-score examples, despite evaluation 169 demonstrating a competitive conventional alternative. What is missing is sustained exploration of that chemistry without repeatedly coupling it to azo chains or mixed heteroatom-rich branches.

The cited upper-score set supplies little evidence of alternative cyclic linkers or new ring heteroatom arrangements. Their contribution to this objective remains untested rather than known to be beneficial.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.548381; its extensively decorated relatives at 284 and 286 score 0.583606 and 0.582950. Amino, thioether and azo substitutions on those aromatic surfaces accompany the higher values. However, the amino/phenol/aldehyde analogue at 169 scores 0.575221 without azo groups, showing that they are not required for the upper observed range. The saturated polyacetal at 47 scores 0.506214, while the quinoline/piperidine analogue with an N-O-rich chain at 24 scores 0.530764. The late indole amide at 297 reaches 0.574024 with a methylthio/azo/amino decoration. These comparisons support locally useful aromatic polar substitution on more than one core; they do not establish that indiscriminately adding heteroatoms improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Most proposals are large, heavily decorated biphenyl compounds joined to an arylsulfonyl pyrrolidine through amide, amine, enamine or aminothiol-containing linkers. The recurring pyrrolidine nitrogen is sulfonylated; it should not be described as an unmasked basic cyclic amine. Extra aniline or aliphatic amino groups appear on the periphery. The best molecule at 273 has a dimethylamino-substituted dichlorophenyl sulfonamide, a difluorobiphenyl group and a chlorinated enamine linker. Evaluation 218 instead supplies an accessible dimethylaminomethyl branch. Mean SMILES length is 84.2, the longest mean in the digest; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9966 and halogen_rate is 0.9862. The underlying sulfonamide/aryl chemistry is recognizable, but many proposed complete structures are encumbered by polyhalogenated appendages and reactive linkers.
liabilities: Chlorinated enamines, sulfenamide/aminothiol motifs and extensively brominated or chlorinated branches complicate stability and synthesis. Fluoroalkyl cumulenes occur late; cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.1414.

Large aromatic surfaces and heavy halogen decoration coexist with several flexible bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. These are liabilities for a tractable series even when the recorded scalar increases.
Neutral input notation must not be mistaken for proof that the molecules are nonionizable, and a docking-task scalar must not be equated with measured receptor affinity.
missing_features: The dominant series does not provide a conventional, independently varied basic cyclic nitrogen: its ring nitrogen remains sulfonylated while additional amines are appended elsewhere. The useful peripheral amine examples motivate a gap in independent control of nitrogen placement and electronic state, not a claim that any cyclic amine would help.

Defined stereoisomers of the substituted pyrrolidine and benzylic/linker centres are absent. Explicitly charged representations are also absent from the submitted strings; whether the evaluation prepared protonated forms internally is not shown.

Chemically ordinary alternatives to the chlorinated enamine and aminothiol linkers, retaining comparable attachment geometry, are missing from the cited upper-score series. Their score effect would require observation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine amide bearing a carboxylic acid at 10 scores 0.0190412. The amine/enamine-bearing analogues at 218 and 273 reach 0.187076 and 0.189601, respectively. Several changes occur together, so the trajectory does not isolate an amine, acid-removal or linker effect. A particularly informative pair is 272 versus 273: relocating fluorines on the distal phenyl ring changes 0.124071 to 0.189601 without changing the main framework or elemental composition. This makes substituent placement an observed distinction beyond simply adding nitrogen or halogens. The quinoline/phenoxy/piperidine compound at 275 scores only 0.00334580 despite a tertiary cyclic amine. Final polyhalogenated/cumulene-containing analogues such as 300 score 0.0677295. The evidence favors particular spatially organized combinations; it supplies no binding pose or interaction assignment.

per_task.generated_character: This trajectory contains the most conventional upper-score chemistry in the supplied set. Better molecules include alkyl-substituted quinolines connected through a methylene ether and phenyl amide to N-alkyl piperidines, alongside diaryl fused diones bearing esters, ethers and alkyl substituents. Evaluation 237 combines a propyl/methyl quinoline, an aryl ether, an amide, an N-methyl piperidine and an aldehyde. Evaluation 102 is an ethyl-substituted diaryl fused dione with an ethyl ester. Elsewhere the trajectory still proposes N-O and N-S chains and branched alkyl growth. These are medium-to-large molecules with mean SMILES length 65.9; aromatic_atom_rate is 1.0, halogen_rate 0.5586 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.0. The main high-score motifs are plausible medicinal-chemistry starting points in outline, with route and stereochemical details unresolved.
liabilities: The highest quinoline example retains an aldehyde, introducing an electrophilic and potentially metabolically sensitive group; its score does not establish acceptable stability.
Long alkyl branches enlarge flexible hydrophobic regions. Early N-O/N-S-rich variants are chemically less ordinary than the upper-score ester/amide series.
Substituted saturated rings and branched chains contain potential stereochemical distinctions that are unspecified in every optimizer string.
missing_features: Many later molecules do not preserve the modest alkyl substitution and simple polar-group balance seen in the better examples; long or branched alkyl additions and further N-alkylation often accompany lower scores. The gap is reliable exploration around chemically economical combinations already demonstrated by the output.

Alternative ring arrangements and defined piperidine/substituent stereochemistry are not represented in the cited upper-score set. The observed modest score differences do not identify a specific absent target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dione at 7 scores 0.167839. Loss of its phenolic OH together with ethyl substitution on an aromatic ring gives 0.175839 at 102 and 0.174613 at 103. The quinoline/piperidine initial molecule at 6 scores 0.156977; the propyl-substituted aldehyde analogue at 237 scores 0.175888. Conventional alkyl/ether/carbonyl patterns therefore characterize the upper observed values. Alkyl extension is not monotonically favorable: the otherwise closely related pentyl quinoline at 282 scores 0.166260, below the propyl compound at 237. N-O-rich derivatives at 18-20 score 0.110506, and the modified flavone at 14 scores 0.112923. The useful distinction is a particular balance and placement of hydrocarbon substituents and conventional polar groups, not unlimited growth or heteroatom-chain elaboration.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules are nonaromatic oxygen-rich polyacetals resembling heavily protected carbohydrate frameworks, decorated with terminal thioaldehydes, other thiocarbonyl groups, aldehydes and chlorinated carbon branches. Evaluation 243 retains the elaborate polyacetal framework while adding repeated terminal thiocarbonyls, an aldehyde and a trichloromethyl substituent. Its near-equal-score relative at 242 redistributes the appendages around the same kind of framework. Other proposals explore hydrazones, N-O chains, sulfur/nitrogen chains and thioketene or longer cumulene appendages; aromatic starting families persist at lower values. Mean SMILES length is 57.6, aromatic_atom_rate is 0.331, halogen_rate 0.5345 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1931. The polyacetal skeleton is recognizable chemistry, but the multiply reactive sulfur-rich products look poor as isolable medicinal compounds without substantial stabilization and synthesis evidence.
liabilities: Repeated terminal thioaldehydes, thioketenes and adjacent thiocarbonyl motifs present substantial chemical-reactivity and isolation concerns. These differ materially from ordinary stable thioamides or sulfones.
The crowded polyacetal framework and multiple oxygen-bearing stereocentres would demand controlled synthesis; no stereochemical assignments or synthetic route are supplied.
Hydrazone/N-O-rich side chains and long cumulated unsaturation recur even among very low-scoring analogues. Rich ring content here does not imply conventional drug-like chemistry.
missing_features: The upper-score series lacks chemically stable alternatives that preserve its favorable balance of ring oxygen, sulfur-containing substituents and chlorinated branches without exposed terminal thioaldehydes or cumulated bonds. Whether a stable replacement preserves the score is unknown.

Conventional basic amines and aromatic nitrogen acceptors are absent from the highest polyacetals, while the earlier aromatic/amine-containing molecules are generally poorer. Their absence can be described, but this trajectory does not support prescribing their addition as this objective's answer.
The stereochemical configurations needed to specify these highly substituted polyacetals are absent from the proposal strings. There is no evidence here of a stereochemically resolved series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial polyacetal at 4 scores 0.0000254690; the extensively sulfur/chlorine-decorated polyacetals at 242 and 243 each score approximately 0.0881235. In contrast, the same broad polyacetal family with hydrazone and O-N appendages at 56 scores 1.23960e-32, and the nitrogen/sulfur-decorated biphenyl amide at 130 scores 1.06523e-33. This supports a narrow favorable combination on the oxygen-rich scaffold, not a general reward for sulfur, heteroatoms or chlorination. The final trichloromethyl/thioketene-containing polyacetal at 296 falls to 1.03025e-09 despite retaining many ostensibly favorable ingredients; the final thiocarbonyl/aldehyde variant at 300 scores 0.00937443. The nearly equal scores for 242 and 243 show tolerance of those particular positional alternatives. No reference molecule or component scores were shown, so the large gradient cannot be assigned to a specific desired pharmacophore or physicochemical term.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Its output repeatedly combines N-F bonds, N-O/N-N chains, sulfur-halogen groups, terminal thioaldehydes and cumulated bonds with otherwise familiar ring frameworks. Cumulated-double-bond rates reach 0.1345, 0.1414 and 0.1931 in the affected proposal sets. A conventional dimethoxy N-methyl indole amide has recorded score 0.395373, while a closely related N-F-bearing analogue scores 0.394920; unusual appendages are therefore not required to reach that observed neighborhood. Conventional amino/phenol/carbonyl and ester/amide examples also coexist with reactive variants.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably keep new substituents within chemically stable functional-group environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add task-independent sensitivity to local bond environments and functional-group compatibility so ordinary amines, ethers, amides and appropriately stabilized sulfur groups remain available without automatically turning into heteroatom chains or reactive endpoints. Preserve structurally comparable stable alternatives and let accepted scalar feedback determine their usefulness.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate is 1.0 for every proposal set, but the repeated indole, fused dione, quinoline/piperidine, arylsulfonyl/pyrrolidine and polyacetal frameworks are recognizable in the supplied initial molecules. The cited maxima remain variations on those frameworks. Across the trajectories, much of the visible novelty lies in pendant chains, exocyclic functionality and substitution positions rather than new cyclic connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring abundance does not translate into demonstrated exploration of substantially different ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator seeking broader chemical coverage would need a way to vary cyclic connectivity, ring heteroatom placement and the connections between ring units, while retaining chemically plausible scaffolds as alternatives. This is a chemical capability gap, not evidence that any particular unseen ring system will improve the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The dominant sulfonylated pyrrolidine series keeps a deactivated ring nitrogen while introducing separate aniline or aliphatic amine centres. Upper-score analogues mix those changes with chlorinated enamine or aminothiol linkers. Relocating distal phenyl fluorines on an otherwise matching framework changes the recorded score from 0.124071 to 0.189601. Conversely, a tertiary cyclic amine on another scaffold has a low recorded score, so nitrogen presence alone does not explain the observed chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output offers limited independent control of functional-group position, basicity and linkage geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support matched changes in attachment position, nitrogen bonding environment and linker type so the search can vary accessible basic centres and molecular geometry independently of adding reactive appendages. Distinguish amines, anilines, amides and sulfonamides as different chemical environments using only the observed scalar feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre_rate and charged_rate are both 0.0 in every proposal set. Nevertheless, the submitted molecules include substituted piperidines and pyrrolidines, benzylic amino centres, fluorinated aminoalkyl branches and complex polyacetals. Several structures contain ionizable amines or acids. These counters establish absent input annotations, not absent molecular stereochemistry or neutral behavior in solution; evaluation-side preparation was not supplied.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express stereochemically resolved or explicitly charged candidate alternatives in these outputs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where the candidate contract supports them, provide chemically justified stereoisomer and ionization-state alternatives and track their identities explicitly. Base the choices on generic chemical rules and accepted observations, without assuming that added stereochemical or charge annotation is itself rewarded.

method_name: Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction
method_thesis: Anchor the method in inverse-QSAR through coupled linear regression and mixed-integer graph construction. [Zhu et al., Sections 1, 3 and 4](https://www.imrpress.com/journal/FBL/27/6/10.31083/j.fbl2706188) encode both a molecular descriptor function and a learned predictor in a program that constructs a graph satisfying structural specifications. Our benchmark adaptation fits a regularized linear score model only to the current objective's accepted observations, using atom-type, degree and typed-bond counts that can be represented exactly by integer constraints. For each proposal, take a scored molecule, choose a bounded editable peripheral region and retain its connected surrounding context. Represent replacement atom identities, bond orders and attachment choices as discrete variables, with connectivity, valence and descriptor-consistency constraints. Maximize the fitted scalar prediction over these variables instead of solving the paper's fixed target-interval problem. A feasible integer assignment supplies the new molecular graph directly. Validate the actual graph and recompute its descriptors before submission; exclude repeated assignments and retry construction when canonical identity is duplicate or invalid. Vary contexts and editable regions as feedback accumulates, and continue construction until the announced batch is filled. Use bounded subproblems and feasible solver incumbents rather than requiring a proof of global optimality for every proposal. The root needs no generative checkpoint or external labels. It constructs atom and bond combinations, without a corpus molecule pool, stored-fragment retrieval or the paper's subsequent isomer-enumeration stage. Each objective starts with clean scored and fitted state. The hypothesis is that jointly enforcing realizable structure while optimizing a task-local prediction concentrates evaluations on improving molecules and raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Exact descriptor realization cannot compensate for an inaccurate predictor; both predictive usefulness and sufficient construction throughput remain unproven.
